paragraphs: Here's what I want you to take with you, friend: a real faith doesn't stay in the building. Paul says the message of the Lord rang out from the Thessalonians, and their faith in God "has gone out to every place" (1 Thessalonians 1:8). Other people were reporting it themselves, so Paul had no need to say anything more (1 Thessalonians 1:8-9). That tells me real faith is the kind that gets noticed AND gets shared.

Now look at how Paul explains it. The gospel came "not only in word, but also in power, in the Holy Spirit, and with great conviction" (1 Thessalonians 1:5). The Thessalonians welcomed it "with the joy of the Holy Spirit, in spite of your great suffering" (1 Thessalonians 1:6). So joy doesn't wait for an easy week, and it's not something you work up on your own. God hands it to you right in the middle of the hard stuff. That's good news for anybody whose week is NOT going great.

And the whole thing points one direction. They turned "to God from idols to serve the living and true God and to await His Son from heaven" (1 Thessalonians 1:9-10). Turning away, serving and waiting all belong together, and Jesus is the One worth waiting on, our "deliverer from the coming wrath" (1 Thessalonians 1:10). So I'd ask you this, baker: what are you turning toward today, and who's watching you do it? Keep the oven warm. Somebody may be learning from you right now.
